caption:
Quinn was sitting on the couch when the room started spinning. No headache, just dizzy spells that kept coming back, until busy shops felt like a rollercoaster and the groceries went online.

Recurring vertigo can be vestibular migraine, even without any headache. It's different from ear-crystal dizziness (BPPV) and is often missed.

What can help: seeing your GP or a neurologist first, keeping a trigger diary for about two months, waking at the same time every day, graded vestibular rehab with head movement and busy visual places, and not letting the dizziness shrink your life.

Get urgent help for a first severe vertigo attack, or dizziness with hearing loss, double vision, slurred speech, weakness or numbness, trouble walking, or after a head injury.
